gradient_identity.assumptions: Fixed x and its logit Jacobian; a hypothetical bounded soft-response distribution with calibrated mean and variance; unweighted BCE.

scalar_Gaussian_counterexample.assumptions: Independent scalar Gaussian latent parameters, known independent Gaussian observation noise, posterior means equal student predictions. This is not a model of Qwen response probabilities.

frozen_batch_direction_counterexample.assumptions: Fixed pre-batch equal priorities and norm-one features; distinct candidate IDs; Gaussian linear model with identity covariance and noise variance .1.

primary_sources.title: Bayesian Active Learning for Classification and Preference Learning
primary_sources.scope: Information about model parameters distinguishes model uncertainty from conditional observation uncertainty; requires a specified posterior and likelihood.

primary_sources.title: Deep Batch Active Learning by Diverse, Uncertain Gradient Lower Bounds
primary_sources.scope: Uses predicted-label final-layer gradient vectors and k-means++ batch diversity; this is prior art and not an RMOT/noisy-Qwen guarantee.

boundaries: The gradient identity is a conditional mathematical identity, not proof that R estimates the required moments.
Magnitude of expected local training gradients is not expected held-out risk reduction, semantic correctness, or HOTA gain.
Actual R/S changes between rounds; only priorities within a selected batch are frozen. The direction example is hypothetical, not a diagnosis of learned real features.
Gaussian posterior information requires known probabilistic assumptions absent from the current deterministic Qwen/R/S setup.
Classic information gain and gradient diversity are not new inventions. Do not rename BALD/BADGE or the existing object-uniform control as our contribution.
No algorithm is changed or selected here. Wait for full186/180 reproduction and registered postseal evidence before a new primary experiment.
